niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” connected-TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand awareness vs direct response), budget, creative needs, measurement/attribution requirements, target markets and which CTV platforms you must reach. Tell me those and I can recommend 2–3 agencies tailored to you. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to pick one plus a short shortlist to consider.

How to choose the right CTV partner
- Primary objective: brand lift/awareness, app installs, e-commerce sales, or direct-response? Different shops specialize in one or more.
- Buying method: programmatic (DSPs) vs guaranteed/direct buys on platforms (Roku/Hulu/YouTube/AVOD/FAST).
- Creative capabilities: do you need dynamic creative, multiple ad lengths, interactive units, or in-stream measurement?
- Measurement & attribution: require cross-screen attribution, incrementality testing, third‑party verification (Nielsen, Samba TV, iSpot)?
- Data & audience: do you need first‑party or third‑party audience targeting, household/addressable targeting, or custom segments?
- Geography & scale: U.S.-only, global, specific countries?
- Budget & campaign length: programmatic scales better for ongoing buys; direct deals often need bigger spend commitments.
- Tech stack & transparency: do you want a full-service agency, a programmatic specialist, or to work directly with platform ad teams?

Shortlist by category (reputable options)
- Global full-service media groups (good for big brand campaigns + cross-channel integration): GroupM (Mindshare, MediaCom, Wavemaker), Omnicom (OMD, PHD), Publicis (Starcom, Zenith), IPG (UM, Initiative), Dentsu (Carat).
- Programmatic / performance specialists (strong with DSPs, audience/data-driven buys): Tinuiti, 3Q Digital, Merkle, Cadreon (IPG programmatic). Also consider independent performance shops that have built CTV capabilities.
- CTV/platform specialists & tech partners (not traditional agencies but often used as partners): Roku Advertising, Hulu/Disney/Peacock ad teams, Amazon Ads, The Trade Desk (DSP — not an agency but central to programmatic CTV buys), Innovid (creative/ad serving/measurement), Tremor/Unruly (video/CTV solutions).
- Measurement & verification partners: Nielsen, Samba TV, iSpot.tv, Moat/Integral Ad Science for viewability/fraud checks.

Questions to ask any agency before hiring
- Which CTV platforms and inventory sources do you use? Programmatic + direct publisher deals?
- Can you show case studies that match my objective (brand lift, installs, ROAS) and industry?
- How do you measure outcomes — can you run incrementality tests and provide third‑party verification?
- What is your tech stack (DSPs, ad server, DMP/identity partners)? Who will own the data?
- What creative services do you provide (dynamic creative, variants, interactive)?
- Minimum spend, fees, campaign reporting cadence, and transparency on media costs?
- Can you guarantee frequency caps, household deduping across devices, and brand safety?

If you want a quick recommendation
- If you’re a national/multinational brand doing cross-channel TV + digital: look first at the global media groups (GroupM, OMD, Starcom, UM).
- If your priority is direct-response performance on a modest or variable budget: look at performance specialists (Tinuiti, 3Q Digital, Merkle) or programmatic teams using The Trade Desk.
- If you need platform expertise / fast direct buys on streaming devices: engage Roku Advertising, Hulu/Disney Ad Sales, or Amazon Ads and pair with a creative/measurement partner like Innovid or Samba TV.

If you share: 1) campaign objective, 2) budget, 3) target geography & audience, and 4) creative needs, I’ll recommend 2–3 specific agencies or partners with the pros/cons of each.
